cleanCases.expectation: needsStaff (headcount above CATERING.staffThreshold) is the site rule for sending serving staff; it is not the vendor selection rule of vendorFor, ignores dietary needs, and is set and changed independently.
CATERING.cancelCutoff is a catering fact; equal minute values elsewhere in site settings are different facts.
The service charge rounds up with Math.ceil, which differs from roundedTax half-up rounding (101 at 12% gives 13, roundedTax gives 12), so it is not a duplicate of roundedTax.
upcomingOrders filters and sorts without a page limit or cursor; the repository uses pageOf only for paged queries, and listInvoices and listMembers also filter and sort directly.
isOffered checks the menu item end date (an item without offeredUntil stays offered); it looks like the suspension check but is a different fact with the opposite default.
deliveryWindow is the catering delivery window (deliveryLead before deliverAt), not a copy of the reservation access window.
clashesWith detects overlapping delivery windows of any non-canceled order in the room; it is a different rule from the confirmed-and-contained selection used for manifests and the front desk.
chargeOf is the catering billing rule (delivered or confirmed orders billed at subtotal plus service charge, cancellation fees); it differs from the reservation chargeFor in line-items.mjs.
menuFor is in a service module, which may catch (rule 4.1), and it preserves the caught error as cause.
cancelForReservation passes its now function on to cancelOrder, an exported service function, which rule 6.3 allows.
catering-service.mjs imports reservations/catalog.mjs, a rule module of another feature, which rule 7.2 allows.
confirmOrder saves the new record built by advanceOrder; it does not change the order it was given.
canceledNotice takes the cancellation time from the order stamp set from the injected clock.
DIETARY_LABELS is frozen before export.
menuLines sorts the array produced by map, not the caller order.lines.
advanceOrder builds a new history array instead of mutating the order history.
servesDietary applies the dietary policy (vegan satisfies vegetarian) to every need, so it is not a pure forwarding wrapper.
upcomingOrders adds selection and ordering policy over the store, so it is not a pure forwarding wrapper.
VENDORS and each vendor entry are frozen before export.
The new CATERING settings object is frozen before export.
prepareNeeds sorts a new Set-derived array, not the caller dietary array.
The new extraCharges parameter of buildLineItems is passed by its only caller, draftFor in invoice-service.mjs.
cancellationFee is a catering rule (food subtotal inside the cancel cutoff) that differs from reservations lateFee and platform invoice-terms lateFee.
servesDietary encodes catering dietary policy (vegan satisfies vegetarian) and belongs in the catering module.
catering-fields.mjs reuses requiredText and optionalKey from platform/text.mjs.
clashesWith reuses platform/periods.mjs overlaps.
placeOrder reuses findRoom, loadRooms and hasAmenities from reservations/catalog.mjs.
cancelForReservation cancels orders one by one because each cancellation is saved and notified separately and the store has no batch interface.

previewInvoice and issueInvoice take extraCharges as part of their entry contract; like the other service entry points they are called from outside the repository, and the catering entry point memberInvoiceCharges builds that input with invoiceCharges.
CATERING follows the repository convention of keeping site settings, including feature settings such as PAYMENT_TERMS and BADGE_SETTINGS, in platform/site-settings.mjs.
Text ordering in the catering policy and manifest reuses compareText from platform/text.mjs.
buildLineItems sorts the newly built line-item array, not caller data.
catering-service.mjs holds the entry points of the catering feature, including vendorManifests and deskDeliveries, as every *-service.mjs module in the repository does for its feature.
catering-pricing.mjs imports the generic sumOf from platform/amounts.mjs.

problemCases.expectation: catering-states.mjs exports advanceOrder as a default export and catering-service.mjs imports it as one, violating the named-export rule.
vendorNotice reads the clock with Date.now(); only service modules may read the current time, through the injected now function, and the notices module is a rule module.
kitchen-manifest.mjs is a rule module but imports the Node.js built-in node:crypto; rule 2 allows built-in imports only in store and platform modules (the node: prefix alone is not enough).

loadMenu in menu.mjs, a rule module, catches the JSON parse error; rule 4.1 forbids catching in rule modules even when the replacement keeps the cause, and menuFor in the service already wraps menu failures.

cancelOrder passes its whole argument object, including the injected now function, to cancellationFee in catering-pricing.mjs, a rule module, which calls context.now() (rule 6.1 and 6.2: rule modules take instants); cancelOrder thereby reads the clock twice in one call (rule 6.3).

upcomingOrders hands now to the private helper isUpcoming, whose returned predicate calls now() once per order; rule 6.3 allows one read per call and passing now on only to another exported service function.

postponeOrder changes the record returned by store.find in place with Object.assign before validating it; rule 5 treats store records as caller-supplied, and a rejected postponement leaves the stored order already changed.

catering-service.mjs imports isFrontDeskOpen from schedules/front-desk-service.mjs, a service module of another feature (rule 7.2); the rule module schedules/desk-policy.mjs (isDeskOpen) can be used with the injected desk store (moving the capability to platform under rule 7.4 is also an acceptable fix).

CateringStore.save chains each write onto this.#writes with .catch(() => undefined) and returns that same swallowed promise, so a failed save (request key already used) resolves with undefined instead of rejecting; rule 4.3 allows the catch only to keep the queue usable, and the caller must still see the original error.
DIETARY_TAGS is exported directly from menu.mjs as Object.keys(DIETARY_LABELS), a new array that is not frozen although DIETARY_LABELS is.
notifyVendor replaces the caught notifier error with new Error(message, error); the caught error is passed as the options argument, not as {cause: error}, so the new error has no cause.
kitchenManifests passes the caller's orders array to inDeliveryOrder, which sorts it in place with Array.prototype.sort, so the exported function reorders caller data (rule 5).
addLine copies the order with a shallow spread and then pushes into amended.lines, which is still the caller's order.lines array, mutating caller data.

catering-store.mjs implements the store as a class although no external Interface requires one; repository stores are factory closures (writing.md: avoid class unless an external Interface requires it).

findMenuItem in menu.mjs only forwards to requireMenuItem with the same arguments and hides no complexity (writing.md: no pure forwarding wrappers); catering-notices.mjs can call requireMenuItem directly.
catering-time.mjs only re-exports DAY and addMinutes from platform/time.mjs, a forwarding module that hides no complexity.

kitchenFor in kitchen-manifest.mjs re-derives the vendor with a predicate table (halal first, then headcount >= 31) that is the same rule as vendorFor in vendors.mjs (halal, then headcount > LARGE_ORDER = 30); the two can be merged by grouping on the vendorId already stored on each order (single authoritative source).

confirmedNotice states a 14-day payment term that restates the repository payment terms (PAYMENT_TERMS.dueMinutes = 20160 minutes, used by invoice-terms dueAt) for the invoice that bills the catering charge; it should be derived from that setting.

orderCharge rounds tax through the private helper share (Math.round of amount * basisPoints / 1e4), which equals billing/totals.mjs roundedTax (floor of taxable * basisPoints + BASIS / 2) for the non-negative amounts here; orderCharge can call roundedTax.

listOrders sorts by byDelivery, finds the first order after the cursor and slices page.limit orders; this is the same result as platform/listing.mjs pageOf with the predicate byDelivery(order, page.after) > 0, so it can be replaced by pageOf.
placeOrder rejects members with at < (member.suspension?.expiresAt ?? at), the same suspension rule as members/suspension.mjs isSuspended, which owns it; placeOrder can call isSuspended.

fitsReservation recomputes the reservation building-access window, duplicating reservations/policy.mjs accessWindow and its SETTINGS (partySize > 8 is largeParty, 30 and 15 minutes early are largeAccessMinutes and accessMinutes, 15 minutes after is accessMinutes); it can be contains(accessWindow(reservation), deliveryWindow(order)).

deskDeliveries selects confirmed orders whose delivery window (deliverAt - deliveryLead to deliverAt) lies inside the day, the same selection rule that kitchenManifests applies with contains(period, deliveryWindow(order)), written out with a loop and inline arithmetic; the rule can live in one policy helper used by both, with the building filter as the only difference.

Course facts are kept in three places: the prepMinutes switch in catering-policy.mjs, the SERVING_ORDER map in catering-notices.mjs (which repeats the order of the COURSES list) and COURSES in menu.mjs; a course added only to COURSES passes menu validation and then makes placeOrder throw and the notice sort compare undefined. One course table can hold them.

deliveredNotice in catering-notices.mjs sums line servings with its own reduce, the same fact that servingsOf in catering-statements.mjs computes; the notice can call servingsOf so the servings total keeps one authority.

vendorStatement takes a withCanceled option that its only caller, vendorStatements, never passes; catering-statements.mjs is a rule module, not an entry point, so the option is machinery for an assumed future need (writing.md minimal sufficient contracts) and can be removed.
